conceptZh: 胖胖的玩具飛機在原地猛催油門、機身抖個不停卻黏在地上；它洩氣地垂下機鼻，這時螺旋槳終於轉對邊，它整台倒著咻一聲飛出去。
object: a chubby toy propeller plane with googly eyes
morph: the glyph 飛 stands still as a solid sculpture while the take-off gag plays out in front of it
creativeAngle: 接上孩子喜歡的戰鬥機與飛行英雄：笑點是「引擎全開卻原地發抖，最後倒著飛走」的方向錯誤。飛的兩組羽狀筆畫最容易被動畫畫錯，所以字體全程不動。語音詞「飛機」，機ㄐㄧ已經學過，兩字都只有一種讀音。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid warm ivory background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 飛 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated deep sky blue, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the tall hooked central stroke and the two matching feather-like groups on the upper left and right stay clearly separated, with every stroke and dot readable. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. In front of its lower right stands a chubby toy propeller plane with googly eyes and stubby wings. From 0.7 seconds it revs hard: the propeller blurs, the whole fuselage shudders and rattles in place, little puffs of effort pop from the tail - and it does not move a single centimetre. The shaking builds until 2.4 seconds, then stops dead. The plane's nose droops forward in disappointment and its googly eyes settle at different heights. Beat. At 3.3 seconds the propeller suddenly spins the other way and the plane shoots backwards out of frame to the right with a cheerful whoosh, tail first, googly eyes spinning. At 4.2 seconds one small screw drops from where it stood, bounces twice and rolls out of shot. From 4.6 to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 飛 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「飛、飛、飛機」, using the reading ㄈㄟ for 飛 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 飛 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 飛機 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 飛: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 消防車想把不聽話的水管舉高，水管卻朝下噴水，把整台車變成空中消防車；隊員終於合作控制方向，飛一小圈後平穩落地。
object: An original chunky toy fire engine with two molded toy firefighter crew members and a mischievous flexible hose.
morph: Keep 飛 as a complete, solid-colored textbook glyph throughout. The hose turns the fire engine into a briefly flying vehicle beside the glyph, illustrating its meaning without altering its strokes.
creativeAngle: 把原先飛機倒退起飛的笑點，改成消防水管反客為主：隊員努力抬水管，結果水管把整台消防車抬上天。以實際離地飛行表現「飛」，完整字形全程保留，避免複雜筆畫變形或混淆。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second original stylized 3D toy animation in one locked, front-facing landscape shot. On a light warm cream background, display the single Traditional Chinese glyph 飛 centered and uncropped, approximately 70% of frame height, with generous margins. Render it in saturated cobalt blue using a correctly formed standard Taiwanese textbook glyph, with crisp, clearly separated strokes and open internal spaces. Preserve this exact glyph silhouette throughout; the animation illustrates its meaning beside it.

In the roomy left margin, stage a chunky coral-red toy fire engine with expressive windshield eyes, two visibly molded toy firefighter figures seated in its open cab, and one flexible hose attached to its side. These are original unbranded toy designs. The engine is eager and overconfident; its hose is cheekily independent. Keep their entire performance outside the glyph silhouette, with no additional props.

At 0.0–1.3 seconds, the engine plants its wheels proudly while both crew members pull together to point the hose upward. The hose bends stubbornly back down. Their arms stretch forward; the engine squints with determination. At 1.3–1.8 seconds, they give one final tug, freeze hopefully, and watch the nozzle curl straight toward the floor. At 1.8 seconds, a soft, compact water jet begins. Instead of lifting the nozzle, its downward thrust lifts the entire fire engine clear of the floor! By 2.5 seconds, all four wheels are dangling and spinning uselessly in the air. Both crew members look down together, then back at the hose; the engine's proud expression becomes a wide-eyed round-mouthed surprise. Keep the ascent slow enough to read, with a clearly separated floor shadow showing actual flight.

From 2.5–3.9 seconds, the crew cooperate to angle the nozzle. The engine makes one small, smooth airborne loop entirely within the left margin, now grinning as it learns to steer. From 3.9–4.6 seconds, they ease the jet down and land gently. The hose curls smugly over the cab while the two crew members sink back into their seats in relief. All water disappears by 4.6 seconds. Hold the complete composition absolutely still from 4.6 through 8.0 seconds: the large centered 飛 remains dominant, and the tiny parked engine rests quietly in the left margin. Never move, stretch, rotate, obscure, or crop the glyph.

Use rounded toy materials, soft studio shadows, bright non-neon colors, and clear visual separation. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「飛、飛、飛機」. Say the first 飛 around 0.4 seconds, the second around 2.9 seconds, and 飛機 around 5.6 seconds during the still hold, with natural pauses and the reading ㄈㄟ throughout. Stop speaking after 飛機. Add only quiet rubber squeaks, a gentle water hiss, and a soft landing sound beneath the voice; no music. The vocabulary is audio only. The sole visible writing is 飛, with no subtitles, labels, numerals, logos, watermarks, unrelated text, clutter, or flashing effects.
